denomProfiles/shakers/tagline: Celibate communal society awaiting Christ's Second Appearing, known for ecstatic worship and craftsmanship.
denomProfiles/shakers/coreDoctrines/0: Christ's Second Appearing was manifested in Mother Ann Lee and continues in the community of Believers.
denomProfiles/shakers/coreDoctrines/1: God is both male and female, Father and Mother.
denomProfiles/shakers/coreDoctrines/2: Celibacy as the way to overcome the root sin of lust.
denomProfiles/shakers/coreDoctrines/3: Confession of sins to elders as the gateway to new life.
denomProfiles/shakers/coreDoctrines/4: Equality of men and women in leadership.
denomProfiles/shakers/focuses/1: Simplicity, honest work and fine craftsmanship.
denomProfiles/shakers/focuses/2: Pacifism and separation from the world.
denomProfiles/shakers/practices/0: Worship with singing and dances, from which the name 'Shakers' derives.
denomProfiles/shakers/practices/2: Parallel male and female leadership of elders and eldresses.
denomProfiles/shakers/practices/3: No sacraments of baptism or communion.
denomProfiles/shakers/influenced/0/text: Shaker furniture and architecture influenced modern design.
denomProfiles/shakers/influenced/1/text: A model for nineteenth-century American utopian communities.
denomProfiles/shakers/keyFigures/1/role: Organised the communities after Lee's death
denomProfiles/swedenborgian-new-church/t: Church built on the visionary writings of Emanuel Swedenborg about God, heaven and the inner sense of Scripture.
denomProfiles/swedenborgian-new-church/c: God is one person, the Lord Jesus Christ, in whom Father, Son and Holy Spirit are three aspects (a trinity of essentials, not persons).
The Last Judgment took place in the spiritual world in 1757, inaugurating the New Jerusalem.
Scripture has an inner, spiritual sense revealed through Swedenborg.
Salvation requires both faith and charity; life after death continues in heaven or hell according to one's love.
Mainstream churches reject its non-trinitarian theology and its claims for Swedenborg's revelations.
denomProfiles/swedenborgian-new-church/f: Education, especially at Bryn Athyn in Pennsylvania.
denomProfiles/swedenborgian-new-church/p: The Holy Supper as a means of conjunction with the Lord.
Women ordained in the General Convention; not in the General Church.
denomProfiles/swedenborgian-new-church/i: Blake, Emerson and others were stimulated by Swedenborg.
Swedenborg's ideas fed nineteenth-century spiritual movements.
denomProfiles/swedenborgian-new-church/k: Organiser of the first New Church in London (1787)
denomProfiles/bible-students/tagline: Independent heirs of Charles Taze Russell's Bible Student movement, outside the Watch Tower Society.
denomProfiles/bible-students/coreDoctrin: God (Jehovah) is supreme; Jesus is the pre-existent Son, not co-equal; the Trinity is rejected.
A ransom sacrifice and restitution for humanity in a coming earthly kingdom.
Mortality of the soul; no eternal torment.
Russell's 'Divine Plan of the Ages' and prophetic chronology.
denomProfiles/bible-students/focuses/0: Bible study, especially Russell's 'Studies in the Scriptures'.
denomProfiles/bible-students/focuses/1: Independent ecclesias free of central authority.
denomProfiles/bible-students/practices/3: Conventions organised by groups such as the Dawn Bible Students Association.
denomProfiles/bible-students/influenced/: Keeps his original teaching in print.
denomProfiles/bible-students/keyFigures/: Founder of the Bible Student movement
Founder of the Laymen's Home Missionary Movement
denomProfiles/worldwide-church-of-god/ta: Herbert W. Armstrong's Sabbath-keeping church, later transformed into an evangelical body.
denomProfiles/worldwide-church-of-god/co: God is a family of two divine beings, Father and Son, into which believers may be born; the Holy Spirit is God's power.
The seventh-day Sabbath and the annual holy days of Leviticus 23 are binding.
British Israelism: the British and Americans descend from the 'lost tribes' of Israel.
Armstrong as God's end-time apostle restoring truth.
These teachings were abandoned by the church under Joseph Tkach Sr in the 1990s.
denomProfiles/worldwide-church-of-god/fo: Broadcasting through The World Tomorrow and publishing The Plain Truth.
Tithing, including second and third tithes.
denomProfiles/worldwide-church-of-god/pr: Observance of Passover, the Feast of Tabernacles and other holy days.
Avoidance of Christmas, Easter and unclean meats.
denomProfiles/worldwide-church-of-god/in: United, Living and Philadelphia Churches of God continue Armstrong's teaching.
denomProfiles/worldwide-church-of-god/ke: Successor who led the doctrinal transformation
denomProfiles/the-pentecostal-mission/ta: White-clad, celibate ministers in faith homes: South Asia's distinctive holiness Pentecostal church.
denomProfiles/the-pentecostal-mission/co: Trinitarian Pentecostal faith with Spirit baptism evidenced by tongues
Entire sanctification and separation from worldly display
Divine healing as the believer's provision, without reliance on medicine
An elect 'Zion' company of overcomers who follow the Lamb (Revelation 14:1–5)
denomProfiles/the-pentecostal-mission/fo: Holiness of life and simplicity of dress
Faith living: ministers receive no salary and solicit no funds
Evangelism through conventions and faith homes
denomProfiles/the-pentecostal-mission/pr: Ministers renounce marriage and possessions and live communally
White clothing for ministers and members at worship; no jewellery
denomProfiles/the-pentecostal-mission/in: Its strict holiness ethos, white dress and plain living shaped expectations across Kerala and Tamil Pentecostal churches.
Tamil, Malayali and Sinhala migrants planted TPM congregations across the Gulf, Europe, North America and Malaysia.
denomProfiles/the-pentecostal-mission/ke: Founder (d. 1945), a Keralite convert from Hinduism
Co-founder in Colombo; later separated from the mission
denomProfiles/the-pentecostal-mission/in: Headquartered at Irumbuliyur, Chennai, it is strong in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, where its white-clad ministers and large conventions are a familiar sight; Bergunder treats it as one of the most distinctive indigenous South Indian Pentecostal bodies.
denomProfiles/believers-eastern-church/t: Evangelical mission church from Kerala that adopted Eastern episcopacy and liturgy.
denomProfiles/believers-eastern-church/c: Nicene Trinitarian faith and evangelical conversion
Episcopacy in continuity with ancient churches
denomProfiles/believers-eastern-church/f: Rural church planting in North India
denomProfiles/believers-eastern-church/i: Its native-missionary model was widely copied by Western support agencies.
Headquartered in Thiruvalla, Kerala, with dioceses across North and South India; its medical college hospital is a major institution in central Travancore.
denomProfiles/st-thomas-evangelical-chur: Kerala's evangelical offshoot of the Mar Thoma Church, formed in 1961.
Guarding against what it sees as a return to pre-reform rites
Lay leader whose lawsuit preceded the separation
Centred on Manjadi, Thiruvalla, in Kerala, with congregations among Malayalis elsewhere in India; Wikipedia gives over 350 congregations.
denomProfiles/tamil-evangelical-lutheran: Tamil Nadu's Lutheran church, rooted in Ziegenbalg's 1706 Tranquebar mission.
The Augsburg Confession and Small Catechism
Real presence in the Lord's Supper
Social service through schools and hospitals
Tamil Protestant traditions from the Tranquebar mission fed into the wider Tamil church, including congregations later in the CSI.
Ziegenbalg's New Testament of 1714 began the Tamil Protestant Bible tradition.
Based in Tiruchirappalli and strongest in the Thanjavur, Tranquebar and Cuddalore districts of Tamil Nadu; it is one of the oldest Protestant churches in Asia.
denomProfiles/andhra-evangelical-luthera: India's largest Lutheran church, born from Father Heyer's 1842 mission in Guntur.
United Evangelical Lutheran Churches in India
As the largest member it has weighed heavily in Indian Lutheran cooperation.
Concentrated in Guntur, Krishna, Godavari and Prakasam districts of Andhra Pradesh; it reports membership in the millions, though published figures vary widely.
denomProfiles/indian-brethren/tagline: Clergy-free Brethren assemblies, strong in Kerala since the 1899 Kumbanad meeting.
denomProfiles/indian-brethren/coreDoctri: Priesthood of all believers without ordained clergy
denomProfiles/indian-brethren/focuses/2: Mission in North India through workers 'commended' by assemblies
denomProfiles/indian-brethren/influenced: Several early Kerala Pentecostal leaders came out of Brethren assemblies and kept their Bible-study style.
Brethren-commended workers planted churches across North India.
denomProfiles/indian-brethren/keyFigures: German missionary and pioneer of Kerala assemblies
Malayalam hymn writer and early leader
denomProfiles/indian-brethren/inIndia: Strongest in central Kerala (Kumbanad, Thiruvalla, Kottayam) and coastal Andhra; Kerala Brethren have sent many workers to North India and the Gulf.
denomProfiles/sharon-fellowship-church/t: Thiruvalla Pentecostal church founded by P. J. Thomas, known for theological training.
denomProfiles/sharon-fellowship-church/f: Evangelism in Kerala and North India
denomProfiles/sharon-fellowship-church/i: Founded by T. G. Koshy, a co-founder of Sharon, it trained many Kerala evangelical leaders.
denomProfiles/sharon-fellowship-church/k: Co-founder; later founder of Faith Theological Seminary
denomProfiles/sharon-fellowship-church/i: Headquartered in Thiruvalla, Kerala, with congregations across India and among Malayalis abroad.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-full-gospel-: Kerala-based Indian branch of the Church of God (Cleveland), founded by Robert F. Cook.
Church of God Declaration of Faith
K. E. Abraham's break with Cook in 1930 led to India's largest indigenous Pentecostal church.
Centred at Mulakuzha in Kerala, with regional organisations in Tamil Nadu and other states.
